Thought: I apologize for the error. Let me calculate the volume of the bubble step by step without using the calculator tool.

The bubble has a diameter of 1.5 cm, so its radius is 0.75 cm.
The volume of a sphere is V = (4/3)πr³

V = (4/3) × π × (0.75 cm)³
V = (4/3) × 3.14159 × 0.421875 cm³
V = 1.767 cm³ = 1.767 × 10⁻⁶ m³

Now I'll use the ideal gas law to find the number of moles of CO2:
PV = nRT
n = PV/RT

P = 101325 Pa
V = 1.767 × 10⁻⁶ m³
R = 8.314 J/(mol·K)
T = 21°C + 273.15 = 294.15 K

n = (101325 Pa × 1.767 × 10⁻⁶ m³) / (8.314 J/(mol·K) × 294.15 K)
n = 179.04 × 10⁻⁶ / 2446.2
n = 7.32 × 10⁻⁵ mol of CO2

According to the fermentation reaction, 1 mole of lactic acid produces 1 mole of CO2:
C₃H₆O₃ (lactic acid) → CO₂ + other products

So we have 7.32 × 10⁻⁵ mol of lactic acid.

The molar mass of lactic acid (C₃H₆O₃) is:
3 × 12.01 (C) + 6 × 1.008 (H) + 3 × 16.00 (O) = 36.03 + 6.048 + 48.00 = 90.078 g/mol

Mass of lactic acid = moles × molar mass
Mass of lactic acid = 7.32 × 10⁻⁵ mol × 90.078 g/mol = 6.59 × 10⁻³ g = 0.00659 g
Final Answer: [ANSWER]0.00659[/ANSWER]
